emergency_line: If you see a downed power line, a fire, or someone is hurt, call 911. Stay at least 35 feet away from downed lines.

safety.text: Treat every downed line as live. Stay at least 35 feet away and keep others away.

Run generators outdoors only, at least 20 feet from the house, exhaust pointed away from doors and windows. Never in a garage or basement. Never plug one into a wall outlet. Use a carbon monoxide alarm.
Never heat your home with a gas oven, stove, or grill.

actions.text: Keep the fridge and freezer closed. Food stays cold about 4 hours in the fridge, 48 hours in a full freezer (24 hours if half full). Throw out perishable food that has been above 40°F for 2 hours or more.
Turn on your phone's low-power mode. Charge from a power bank, or in a car only when it's outdoors, never in a garage.
Unplug electronics so they aren't damaged when power returns.

needs_actions.text: Keep insulin in its box, away from heat and from freezing. Many insulins are OK at room temperature (59-86°F) for up to 28 days, but it varies by brand, so check the label or ask your pharmacist. If you use a cooler, don't let insulin touch ice. Don't use insulin that has frozen.

assumptions: Guidance is chosen by expected outage length and the needs you told us. We don't guess anything about you.
what_would_change: A longer estimate adds more steps to this list.
